title: नेपालमा उच्च शिक्षाका नेताको नेतृत्व संसार
nepali: उच्च शिक्षामा सक्रिय सहभागीका रूपमा प्राध्यापक, कर्मचारी र विद्यार्थीहरू रहेका हुन्छन् । उच्च शैक्षिक संस्थाका रूपमा नेपालमा बाह्रवटा विश्वविद्यलयहरूका साथमा आङ्गिक र सम्बन्धन प्राप्त क्यम्पसहरू सञ्चालनमा छन् । क्याम्पसका प्रमुखहरू आवश्यकताका आधारमा प्राध्यापक, कर्मचारी र विद्यार्थीहरूको सरसहयोग लिनुपर्ने कुरा यसको सञ्चालनसम्बन्धी नीतिगत व्यवस्था गरिएको छ । त्यस्तै क्याम्पसमा प्राध्यापक, कर्मचारी र विद्यार्थीहरूका हक अधिकारका निम्ति आआफ्नै पेसागत सङ्घ र सङ्गठनहरू भएकाले त्यसको नेतृत्व राजनीतिबाट टाढा रहन सक्दैन । यस अध्ययनको उद्देश्य उच्च शिक्षाका शैक्षिक नेतृत्वको व्यक्तिगत, सामाजिक र राजनीतिक पेसागत भोगाई अनुभवको अध्ययन गर्नु रहेको छ । उच्च शैक्षिक संस्थाअन्तर्गत त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालयको क्याम्पसको नेतृत्व सम्हालेका शैक्षिक तथा प्रशासनिक नेतृत्व लिएका एक शैक्षिक प्रशासक नेताले भोगेका व्यक्तिगत अनुभव संसारको बारेमा न्यारेटिभ विधिद्वारा कथाको विकास गरिएको छ । उनलाई उद्देश्यमूलक नमुना छनोट विधिका आधारमा छनोट गरिएको छ । त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालयमा पनि नेपालका अन्य प्रशासनिक क्षेत्रमा जस्तै राजनीति भागबन्डाबाट पदाधिकारीको पदस्थापन गरिन्छ । शिक्षक, कर्मचारी, विद्यार्थी र सहकर्मीहरूको उच्च शिक्षामा नेतृत्वलाई समर्थन वा विरोध, व्यक्तिगत वा साङ्गठनिक स्वार्थका आधारमा व्यक्त हुन्छ । नेतृत्वको व्यवहार पनि आफ्नो राजनैतिक बिचार वा दर्शनद्वारा शक्ति प्राप्त गरिएको हुन्छ । अनुभव र दर्शनले उनको नेतृत्वलाई निर्देशित गर्दछ । पार्टीगत वा साङ्गठनिक निर्णयलाई प्राथमिकता राखेर निर्णय गर्दा उच्च शिक्षाको नेतृत्व भने विवाद रहित हुन नसकेको पाइयो । मास्लोको आत्मसम्मान र आत्मबोध प्राप्त गर्न उच्चशैक्षिक नेतृत्वमा कठिनाइ हुँदो रहेछ । तर, रूपान्तरित नेतृत्वमा सामान्य मात्र प्राध्यापक, कर्मचारी र विद्यार्थीको सहयोग, समन्वय र परिस्थितिले समेत सहयोग गरेको अवस्थामा क्याम्पसको विकास र रूपान्तरण सम्भव हुँदो रहेछ ।
american_english: Professors, staff, and students are present as active participants in higher education. As higher educational institutions, along with twelve universities, constituent and affiliated campuses operate in Nepal. A policy provision regarding their operation has been made that campus chiefs must take the cooperation of professors, staff, and students on the basis of necessity. Similarly, because professors, staff, and students have their own professional unions and organizations for their rights on campus, their leadership cannot remain far from politics. The objective of this study is to study the personal, social, and political-professional lived experiences of educational leadership in higher education. Through the narrative method, a story has been developed regarding the world of personal experiences lived by an educational administrator-leader who assumed educational and administrative leadership of a campus under the higher educational institution Tribhuvan University. He was selected on the basis of the purposive sampling method. At Tribhuvan University as well, just as in other administrative sectors of Nepal, officials are appointed through political power-sharing. The support or opposition of teachers, staff, students, and peers toward leadership in higher education is expressed on the basis of personal or organizational interests. The behavior of leadership too derives power from its own political ideology or philosophy. Experience and philosophy guide his leadership. When making decisions giving priority to partisan or organizational decisions, higher education leadership was found unable to remain free of controversy. Achieving Maslow's self-esteem and self-actualization turns out to be difficult in higher educational leadership. However, in transformational leadership, when even ordinary cooperation and coordination from professors, staff, and students and circumstances provide support, the development and transformation of the campus turns out to be possible.

informal_english: Professors, staff, and students are all active participants in higher education. For higher educational institutions in Nepal, twelve universities operate alongside constituent and affiliated campuses. Operating policy sets down that campus chiefs have got to take the help and cooperation of professors, staff, and students based on necessity. Similarly, because professors, staff, and students have got their own professional unions and organisations batting for their rights on campus, that leadership can't stay far from politics. The whole aim of this study is to look into the personal, social, and political-professional lived experiences of educational leaders in higher education. Through the narrative method, a story was developed about the personal experiential world lived by an educational administrator-leader who took on academic and administrative leadership of a campus under Tribhuvan University. He was picked out on the basis of purposive sampling. At Tribhuvan Uni as well, just like other administrative sectors in Nepal, officials get appointed through political power-sharing quotas. Support or opposition from teachers, staff, students, and peers towards higher ed leadership gets expressed based on personal or organisational interests. The behaviour of leadership too draws its power from its own political ideology or philosophy. Experience and philosophy guide his leadership. When making decisions by prioritising party or organisational calls, higher education leadership couldn't stay clear of controversy. Hitting Maslow's self-esteem and self-actualisation turns out to be pretty tough in higher educational leadership. Still, in transformational leadership, when even normal cooperation and teamwork from professors, staff, and students and circumstances lend a hand, developing and transforming the campus turns out to be completely doable.
